title: Credential lifecycle and observability acceptance workbook for Private Deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidated acceptance workbook that defines requirements, test scenarios, evidence artifacts, and sign-off criteria for credential lifecycle, SSO/SAML assertions, RBAC model verification, audit log fidelity, and KMS/HSM operational controls in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. This ticket scopes alignment across PM, Security, SRE, and Engineering for operator onboarding and customer audit readiness.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Customers can configure IdP metadata and complete SAML federation end-to-end. Assertion attributes (email, nameID, groups) map to Redwood identities and group-to-role mapping is demonstrably applied.

SAML: Signed assertions validated against customer certificate chain; test cases include expired cert, invalid signature, replayed assertion and assertion audience mismatch all failing with proper 4xx/401 responses and audit records.

RBAC: Role model supports at minimum: viewer, operator, admin, billing-admin. Each role's permissions are enumerated and enforced. Automated tests verify permission denials for actions outside role scope (e.g., viewer cannot rotate KMS keys).
RBAC: Support for attribute-based access controls via group mappings from SAML; tests include group add/remove propagation and immediate enforcement within 60s of change.

Audit logs: All credential events (login, SAML assertion accepted/failed, role changes, KMS key creation/rotation, key usage, HSM fallback events) are emitted with timestamp, actor, request_id, and outcome. Logs are immutable and tamper-evident for retention period configured per customer.
Audit retention: Configurable retention policy per customer with default 365 days; automated export to customer S3/GCS or secure archival path available and verified via sample export run.

KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys supported with wrap/unwrap semantics. Key rotation policy can be scheduled and performed with zero downtime; test rotation across primary and replica HSMs without rejected decrypts for in-flight requests.
KMS: KMS access control restricts key usage to authorized operator identities; attempts by unauthorized identities are rejected and logged.
Emergency key escrow: Documented, tested key-escrow and recovery procedure with multi-approver workflow; end-to-end runbook executed in staging with captured evidence.
Observability: Console surface shows per-tenant key usage metrics, SAML login success/failure rates, RBAC change history, and audit log search with filters for actor, event_type, and time range.

E2E tests: Automated CI scenarios that spin a private deployment environment, configure SAML IdP (SAML test harness), exercise RBAC role changes, rotate keys, and assert that audit evidence and metrics are produced and stored.

Performance: Instrumentation for audit pipeline shows ingestion latency <10s for write-through logs under baseline load; when ingestion backlog occurs a durable buffer persists events and signals alarms to SRE.

Compliance evidence: For a sample customer onboarding, produce a signed evidence package containing configuration snapshots, audit log extracts for requested time windows, KMS rotation logs, and operator approvals.
Docs & Runbooks: Runbooks for operator onboarding, key rotation, emergency key-escrow, SAML onboarding checklist, and audit evidence export are published and linked from the console.
Security review: All cryptographic operations and key management design have a completed security review and threat-model doc attached.
Backward compatibility: Existing Private customers must be able to upgrade without forced key rewraps; migration steps and compatibility tests documented and executed.
Sign-off: Each acceptance item must have a named owner and evidence artifact (link to log extract, PR, test run, or video) attached before sign-off by Security, PM, and Engineering.
signoff_checklist: PM validates requirements and confirms acceptance criteria coverage (Aisha Patel)
Security signs off on crypto design, HSM integration, and threat model (Security Lead)
Engineering verifies API behavior, RBAC enforcement tests, and KMS/HSM integration (Liam Chen)
SRE confirms audit pipeline durability, alerting, and operational playbooks (SRE Lead)
Legal/Compliance acknowledges evidence package format and retention commitments (Legal Counsel)
Customer Ops proves export workflow with a sample customer export (Customer Ops).
UX/Console team verifies observability surfaces and export UX (Design Reviewer)
Runbook drills completed: emergency key-escrow and operator onboarding exercises documented (runbook evidence link)
Automated CI runs green for E2E onboarding, RBAC, and KMS scenarios (CI link)
Final sign-off meeting recorded with minutes and action items resolved (meeting link)
Create a post-release validation ticket to monitor first 3 production upgrades for regressions (PM follow-up)
Attach evidence artifacts (at least one log extract, one key rotation trace, one PR, and one runbook video) prior to marking Done
implementation_notes: Prefer customer KMS integration via standard KMIP or cloud provider KMS connectors; provide HSM shim for on-prem customers where KMIP is unavailable.
Introduce an immutable audit-event envelope that includes request_id, canonical_actor_id, tenant_id, and event_hash to detect tampering during ingestion and at rest.
RBAC implementation will use a versioned role-schema; service enforces role version in token introspection to allow staged rollouts of permission changes.
SAML onboarding helper: provide a step-by-step UI with test assertion generator and a telemetry endpoint to validate assertions before enabling in production.
Provide nightly export smoke-tests and a manual export feature with role-gated access for Customer Ops and Compliance auditors.
Plan for a staged rollout: feature-flag the advanced observability UI and KMS customer import, begin with internal beta, then invite 3 reference customers for early validation.
Estimate coordination work with infra team for HSM procurement and with legal for updated contractual language on key custody and retention.
Document fallback behavior when HSM is unreachable: service should fail closed for key-creation and fail open for read-only decrypts only if explicitly authorized with documented risk acceptance.
All produced artifacts (PRs, runbook videos, SAML test harness configs) must be referenced in the evidence package for sign-off.
rollout_notes: Beta cohort: 3 reference customers with varying deployment topologies (VPC, air-gapped, on-prem).
Duration: 6-week beta with weekly review checkpoints and automated health dashboards shared with customers.
Fallback: Canary with automatic rollback if audit ingestion errors exceed threshold or if unauthorized access attempts spike.
Support: 24/7 on-call support during the first 2 weeks of GA for migration issues.
Communication: Customer-facing onboarding checklist, and privacy/compliance FAQ to be published at GA launch.
